Awesome AI for Economists 

 
 

A curated list of AI tools, agent skills, libraries, and resources for economics research, teaching, and policy analysis.

 Scope: AI tools and resources with specific value for economists, plus research on the economics of AI. General-purpose AI assistants and coding agents are in the Appendix.

 
 Highlights: Projects from the OpenEcon team, which maintains this list. Entries in bold below are the team's own.
 
 - [ AI-research-setup ][ai-research-setup] - Step-by-step guide to setting up Claude Code and Codex for economics research on macOS and Windows. 
 - [ OpenEcon Data ][openecon-data] - MCP server and web app for plain-English queries over 330,000+ indicators from FRED, World Bank, IMF, Eurostat, and more. 
 - [ Stata-MCP ][stata-mcp] - Runs Stata from VS Code, Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, and Copilot with real-time output, a data viewer, and graph display. 
 - [ Econ Writing Skill ][econ-writing-skill] - Economics paper-writing skill synthesizing 50+ guides by Cochrane, McCloskey, Shapiro, Head, and others. 
 - [ Econ Paper Review Skill ][econ-paper-review-skill] - Writes referee reports on economics papers with verified comments, editing notes, and a step-by-step revision plan; free for non-commercial use. 
 - [ Econ Slides Skill ][econ-slides-skill] - Turns a paper into a Beamer talk with a timed speaker script, including job-market and discussant decks. 
 - [ overleaf-sync-now ][overleaf-sync-now] - Agent skill and CLI that pull recent Overleaf web edits into a Dropbox-synced copy before AI agents edit it. 
 - [ Econ Auto Research ][econ-auto-research] - Vision-stage plan (no code yet) for an economist-directed AI pipeline from research question to working paper, with adversarial self-refereeing.

 MCP Servers for Economic Data

Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers let AI assistants query economic databases directly. Connect Claude, Cursor, or other MCP-compatible tools to live data from FRED, World Bank, IMF, and more.

- Data Commons MCP Server - Official Data Commons server, hosted with a free key or run locally, serving Census, World Bank, BLS, and WHO statistics. 
- ECB MCP Server - Query European Central Bank exchange rates, policy rates, yield curves, and euro-area monetary statistics. 
- Equibles MCP - Self-hosted, open-source server for SEC filings, XBRL financials, 13F holdings, insider trades, short interest, CFTC positioning, and federal contracts. 
- Eurostat MCP Server - Search, inspect, and query Eurostat datasets, including Comext detailed trade, PRODCOM, and NUTS regional data. 
- FRED MCP Connector - St. Louis Fed's official connector letting AI assistants search, fetch, and chart FRED series; requires only a free account.
- FRED MCP Server - Community open-source FRED server run with your own free API key; a self-hostable alternative to the official connector. 
- IMF Data MCP Server - WEO forecasts, balance of payments, and more from the IMF. 
- Invokely - Hosted server for official U.S., EU, UK, Canadian, and Australian statistics, down to U.S. counties and Spanish municipalities.
- MoSPI eSankhyiki MCP - Official Indian statistics ministry server for PLFS, CPI, national accounts, NSS surveys, and more. 
- Nasdaq Data Link MCP - Access Nasdaq/Quandl financial and economic datasets. 
- OECD MCP Server - Access 5,000+ OECD statistical datasets via SDMX API with prompt templates. 
- OpenEcon Data - MCP server and web app for plain-English queries over 330,000+ indicators from FRED, World Bank, IMF, Eurostat, and more. 
- SEC EDGAR MCP - Connects AI assistants to U.S. SEC EDGAR filings, financial statements, and insider-trading data. 
- StatCite - World Bank, IMF, and ECB statistics where every value carries a full citation, plus verification of claimed figures. 
- U.S. Census Bureau Data API MCP - Official Census Bureau server connecting AI assistants to demographic, economic, and population statistics. 
- UN Comtrade MCP Server - Access UN Comtrade international trade statistics with country and HS commodity code lookup. 
- World Bank Data360 MCP - Official World Bank server with a public hosted endpoint (no key needed) for searching, fetching, and charting Data360 indicators. 
- World Bank MCP Server - Community server for the legacy World Bank Open Data API (the official one is World Bank Data360 MCP above). 

 Browse the MCP Registry to discover more servers.

 Agent Skills for Economists

Agent Skills are folders that an AI agent loads when a task needs them: a SKILL.md file of instructions, plus optional scripts and reference files. The open format works in Claude, Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and other agents.

- AI Research Feedback - Claes Bäckman's (SAFE Frankfurt) skills for multi-agent referee reports plus pre-analysis-plan, grant, and replication-code reviews. 
- Awesome Journal Skills - Per-journal skill packs for AER, QJE, the AEJs, and hundreds of other venues, from topic choice to referee response. 
- awesome-econ-ai-stuff - Antonio Mele's (LSE) SKILL.md collection for Stata, R, and Python econometrics, data fetching, LaTeX tables, literature review, and modeling. 
- Claude Code Academic Workflow - Pedro Sant'Anna's (Emory) ready-to-fork template with 60+ ski

usage.html:
• AI-Assisted Teams Outperform AI-Led Teams but Not Human-Only Teams in Assessing Research Reproducibility in Quantitative Social Science - Brodeur et al. (2026), Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
  • Teaching Economics to the Machines - Chen et al. (2026), NBER Working Paper 34713.
  • Performing Valid Inference with AI/ML-Generated Covariates: A Guide for Empirical Practice - Christensen and Hansen (2026), AEA Papers and Proceedings.
  • A Practitioner's Guide to Using Large Language Models and Generative AI in Economic History - Ferrara (2026), NBER Working Paper 35374.
  • Large Language Models: An Applied Econometric Framework - Ludwig, Mullainathan, and Rambachan (2026), Annual Review of Economics.
  • Machine Learning Who to Nudge: Causal vs Predictive Targeting in a Field Experiment on Student Financial Aid Renewal - Athey, Keleher, and Spiess (2025), Journal of Econometrics.
  • Artificial Intelligence in Economics Research: What Have We Learned? What Do We Need to Learn? - Bahoo et al. (2025), Journal of Economic Surveys.
  • Deep Learning for Economists - Dell (2025), Journal of Economic Literature.
  • Difference-in-Difference Causal Forests with an Application to Payroll Tax Incidence in Norway - Gavrilova, Langørgen, and Zoutman (2025), Journal of Applied Econometrics.
  • AI Agents for Economic Research - Korinek (2025), NBER Working Paper 34202.
  • Economics in the Age of Algorithms - Mullainathan (2025), AEA Papers and Proceedings.
  • Machine Learning as a Tool for Hypothesis Generation - Ludwig and Mullainathan (2024), Quarterly Journal of Economics.
  • Large Language Models as Simulated Economic Agents: What Can We Learn from Homo Silicus? - Horton, Filippas, and Manning (2023), NBER Working Paper 31122.
  • Generative AI for Economic Research: Use Cases and Implications for Economists - Korinek (2023), Journal of Economic Literature.
  • Machine Learning Methods That Economists Should Know About - Athey and Imbens (2019), Annual Review of Economics.
  • Text as Data - Gentzkow, Kelly, and Taddy (2019), Journal of Economic Literature.
  • Machine Learning: An Applied Econometric Approach - Mullainathan and Spiess (2017), Journal of Economic Perspectives.
